how.title: Signals in　Orders out
how.lede: From the moment a signal is published, the system takes over.
how.s1.title: A professional publishes
how.s1.body: The provider posts gold entry and exit levels in the group. The central capture machine reads it, then parses direction, entry, stop loss and every take-profit level.
how.s2.title: The cloud fans it out
how.s2.body: The parsed signal goes straight to the cloud hub and reaches every member at once — nobody is served first. Deduplication and a freshness lock keep stale signals from being filled late.
how.s3.title: Your MT5 fills it
how.s3.body: The member client polls every second and places the order on your local MT5 using your own lot sizes and strategy. Lot sizing, martingale and risk limits are all decided on your machine.
feat.title: Every knob　is yours
feat.lede: Copying the signal isn't the whole job. Everything that moves your P&L is left for you to turn.
feat.martingale.title: Martingale ladder engine
feat.martingale.body: Set the multiplier, the maximum number of steps and a custom lot size per step. Each signal source counts its own ladder, so one losing streak never drags another source down. Reset by hand at any time.
feat.partial.title: Scaled exits and break-even stops
feat.partial.body: Close in proportional tranches across several take-profit levels, or switch to moving the stop to entry as soon as the first target prints. Chosen per source, independently.
feat.sources.title: Per-source control
feat.sources.body: Follow or ignore each source, run martingale or flat sizing, set its own lot size. Disabled sources take up no screen space and are excluded from the statistics.
feat.risk.title: Daily risk ceiling
feat.risk.body: Set a maximum daily loss as an amount or a percentage; crossing it stops trading. Pending orders that sit unfilled past your timeout are cancelled automatically, and MT5 is told to delete the order.
feat.schedule.title: Scheduling
feat.schedule.body: Set the hours to start and stop automatically. Outside market hours the clock pauses on its own — leaving the app open does not burn your plan time.
feat.report.title: Live performance reporting
feat.report.body: Today, this week and this month: equity curve, win rate, profit factor and per-source breakdown. Another EA running on the same account can be tagged and folded into the same statistics.

faq.title: Ask first
faq.q1: Does my computer have to stay on?
faq.a1: Yes. The member client has to be running on your machine and MT5 has to stay logged in, otherwise there is nothing to place the order when a signal arrives. The upside: plan time is only deducted while the system is actually running, and it pauses itself outside market hours.
faq.a2: Any broker that offers MetaTrader 5. The system writes order instructions into the file bridge directory of your own local MT5, and an EA attached to the chart executes them. Nothing passes through a third-party account — your funds stay with your broker throughout.
faq.q3: Can a signal be missed or filled twice?
faq.a3: There are three guards. Deduplication persists across restarts of the program. A freshness lock stops stale signals from being filled late. After a restart the client reclaims positions that already exist in MT5 rather than opening them again. When one source revises an order within a short window, only the latest version is followed.
faq.q4: What is the risk with martingale?
faq.a4: Martingale adds size after each loss, so in theory one win recovers the earlier losses — but if price keeps moving against you, the loss is magnified substantially. The system lets you cap the number of steps, the lot size at each step and the maximum daily loss, and it stops on its own when a limit is hit. That is risk control, not a guarantee. Only commit money you can afford to lose entirely.
faq.a5: You buy a balance of usable time, not calendar days. The clock does not run while the system is stopped, and it pauses outside market hours. Buying a full year adds two extra months of time to the balance.

faqp.metaTitle: FAQ and support — AI Gold Copy Trading
faqp.metaDesc: How copying works, the risks, plan billing, installation, and how to reach us.
faqp.title: Ask first
faqp.lede: Everything people ask, written down. Anything else, send us a message.
faqp.a6: They come from independent third-party providers who post gold entry and exit levels in their own groups. We capture them, parse them into structured order instructions, and send those to your MT5. We do not generate the signals and are not responsible for their accuracy.
faqp.q7: How long from publication to fill?
faqp.a7: The central capture machine parses the signal and pushes it to the cloud hub immediately; the client polls once a second. End-to-end latency is usually a few seconds. The actual fill also depends on your network, your broker's servers and the liquidity at that moment.
faqp.q8: Can I follow only one source?
faqp.a8: Yes. Every source is its own set of settings — follow or ignore, martingale or flat, and how much. A disabled source disappears from the layout and is excluded from the statistics.
faqp.a9: No. Every order instruction is generated on your own computer, written into your local MT5's file bridge directory, and executed by the EA attached to your chart. Funds stay within the account relationship between you and your broker throughout. We never handle, hold, or move them.
faqp.q10: What is the most I can lose?
faqp.a10: There is no guaranteed ceiling. You can set a maximum daily loss as an amount or a percentage and the system stops when it is hit, but that is a soft control, not a guarantee — gaps, slippage and extreme moves can all push the realised loss past your setting. Margin trading can cost you your entire capital. Only commit money you can afford to lose completely.
faqp.q11: Can I stop at any time?
faqp.a11: Yes. Press Stop and no new signals are taken. Positions already open are not closed automatically; you decide in MT5 whether to hold or close them.
faqp.a12: Message us on Instagram to arrange it. Once your account is opened you receive a username and password to sign in with.
faqp.a13: Yes. Contact us to upgrade or downgrade. The change takes effect immediately on the device you are signed in on — no reinstall needed.
faqp.a14: One device online at a time. Signing in on a new machine signs the old one out, so the same signal is never placed twice.
faqp.a15: MetaTrader 5 only. The system relies on MT5's file bridge and its EA to place orders; there is no MT4 equivalent implemented.
faqp.q16: Why does MT5 show as disconnected?
faqp.a16: Usually one of three things: MT5 is closed or not signed in, the EA is not attached to a chart, or Allow algorithmic trading is unticked. The client's status log names the file it cannot read, which normally points straight at the cause.
faqp.q17: Can I run two copy accounts on one machine?
faqp.a17: Yes — start the second one with the --instance flag and its settings and records stay entirely separate. Each MT5 account still maps to exactly one client.
faqp.contactBody: Send us a message with what you are seeing. Include the error text if there is one — it speeds things up considerably.
faqp.contactHours: Response time depends on volume, usually within one business day
